single-agent.title: Incomplete support for WebSocket denial responses in all response types
single-agent.message: The logic for prefixing ASGI message types with 'websocket.' is only added to the base Response class. Other response types that override __call__, such as StreamingResponse and FileResponse, have not been updated. Consequently, using a StreamingResponse or FileResponse as a denial response will result in incorrect ASGI message types (e.g., 'http.response.start' instead of 'websocket.http.response.start'), which will cause a RuntimeError in the WebSocket state machine.
single-agent.evidence: prefix = "websocket." if scope["type"] == "websocket" else ""

single-agent.title: Potential AttributeError in WebSocketDenialResponse
single-agent.message: WebSocketDenialResponse inherits from both httpx.Response and WebSocketDisconnect. Since httpx.Response.__init__ is called first and does not invoke super().__init__, WebSocketDisconnect.__init__ is never executed. This results in instances of WebSocketDenialResponse lacking the 'code' and 'reason' attributes expected of a WebSocketDisconnect exception, which will cause an AttributeError if they are accessed in error handling code.
single-agent.evidence: class WebSocketDenialResponse(httpx.Response, WebSocketDisconnect):

suggestion.rationale: Adding an __init__ method ensures that the 'code' and 'reason' attributes are initialized, maintaining compatibility with code that catches WebSocketDisconnect and expects these attributes to be present.

single-agent.title: Potential infinite recursion
single-agent.message: If a server inconsistently reports range support (e.g., fails a range request but includes 'Accept-Ranges: bytes' in a full GET response), this method will enter an infinite recursion loop. It attempts the lazy fetch, fails, falls back to full download, detects range support, and retries the lazy fetch indefinitely.
single-agent.evidence: return self._get_info_from_wheel(link.url)

suggestion.rationale: Tracking whether a lazy attempt was already made for the current call prevents infinite recursion if the server's range support reporting is inconsistent.

single-agent.title: Incorrect seek position in ensure_downloaded
single-agent.message: The loop seeks to the beginning of the entire requested range ('start') for every missing interval, instead of seeking to the start of each specific interval ('range_start'). This causes data corruption in the backing file as subsequent intervals overwrite previous ones at the wrong offset.
single-agent.evidence: self.seek(start)

suggestion.rationale: The file pointer must be moved to the start of the specific interval being written to ensure data is placed at the correct offset in the backing file.
